texts.orig: Farmed Litopenaeus vannamei in intermolt state (Chan et al , 1988) and weighing 25 g, were kept in 1500 L circular flat bottom tanks at 28*C, 3090 salinity, and oxygen saturation. Organisms were fed twice at 8:00 and 17.00 with PIASA feed: 409 protein; 79 lipid, 39 fiber; 129 water 119 ash, and 279 free nitrogen extract. Organisms were starved for 24 h prior to trypsinogen testing by Western blot. Organisms   were decapitated, and the midgut glands were excised  and homogenized in acetone 2:1 (v:w) at 4C to precipitate proteins. The precipitate was dissolved in 20 mM ethylenediamine-tetraacetic acid (EDTA in Laemmli sample buffer, and analyzed immediately. For immunohistology, one group of 40 organisms was starved 24 h, and a second group of 40 was killed 3 h after feeding. day

texts.orig: Midgut glands of 40 fed and 40 starved   organisms were dissected and fixed for 36 h in formaldehyde diluted to 3.79 with seawater. Fixed tissues were dehydrated in increasing concentrations of ethanol at room temperature  and embedded in paraffin. Serial cuts of 3 um were obtained from each gland. Slices were mounted on glass slides and dried for 16 h at room temperature_ After paraffin removal  with xylol and passage through another   dehydration series sections were  treated cells stained with hematoxylin-eosin, anti-TAP and anti-IP antibodies diluted 1.200 in PBS for 2 h at room temperature Controls were incubated with normal rabbit serum, with first antibody  omitted or blocked with its antigen (Harlow and Lane, 1988). After thorough with PBS, sections were incubated with anti-rabbit-HRP diluted 1.3000 in PBS. Finally , sections were washed with PBS. Antibody-reactive molecules were indicated by chromogenic reaction of HRP (Harlow and Lane, 1988). Photos were taken with light microscope at 20X magnification (BX4I Olympus) Images were obtained with a 1.4 megapixel CoolSNAP-Pro cooled CCD camera, utilizing Image-Proplus 4.1 Olympus software midgut rinsing

The figures show transverse 3-um   paraffin serial sections of midgut glands. Cell type was classified according to Bell and Lightner The B cells   contained one  very vacuole; typically having a highly convex lumen surface, and the nucleus was displaced peripherally toward the basal region of the cell. texts.orig: The SDS-PAGE of midgut   gland extract showed a complex protein composition, related to both size and concentration (Fig. 2, Lane I). Western   blots  for the same extract   displayed three bands (Mr 29.7,30.2, and 32.9) when anti TAP  antibodies were (Fig. 2, Lane   II). Two proteins were displayed when using anti-IP antibodies   against   the crude extract (Fig. 2, Lane III) . The molecular mass of the two proteins was the same as those of  the two heavier   proteins displayed by the anti-TAP antibodies (30.2 and 32.9 kDa) The anti-TAP antibodies detected no protein when extracts were not prepared by precipitation with acetone No signal was observed when blots were treated with control sera Or with antibodies previously incubated with synthesized peptides: used

texts.orig: The   80 shrimp analyzed  presented   reactive molecules with both anti-peptide antibodies only in   secretory B and starved organisms (Figs. 3 4). The figures show equivalent areas of serial cuts, although the pictures   displayed (B, C, and D) are slightly displaced. When animals were fed (Fig. 4), it was possible to recognize feed in the lumen. Some B cells in both corresponding   positions were stained   with the antibodies (Figs. 4B, C), and the feed serum blocked by the respective antigen (IP or TAP) showed no positive result (Figs. 3D, 4D).
